data.lede: Northgate Industrial JSC is a full-cycle general contractor: design, steel frame, envelope, building services and turnkey handover. Our own steel fabrication plant in Vorsino, four regional divisions, 1,240 people on staff.

data.title: Privacy
data.lede: How Northgate Industrial collects and uses personal data received through this website, and the rights you have over it.

children.text: 1. What we collect

We collect only what a request needs. The request form asks for your name, company, e-mail, phone and a description of the project, plus any drawings you attach. The newsletter form asks for an e-mail address. The careers page passes the role you chose to the contact form; a CV sent to our HR address is kept with the application.
The site records the usual technical data of a visit — IP address, browser, pages viewed and the time of the visit — in server logs.
2. Why we use it
We process this data to:
answer a request for a quote or a site survey and prepare an estimate;
send the newsletter you subscribed to, with an unsubscribe link in every issue;
consider a job application and contact you about it;
keep the site secure and understand which pages are used.
3. How long we keep it

Request data is kept for the time needed to answer and, where a contract follows, for the life of the contract and the statutory retention period after it. Newsletter addresses are kept until you unsubscribe. CVs are kept for one year after the vacancy closes unless you ask us to delete them sooner. Server logs are kept for 90 days.
4. Who we share it with

We do not sell personal data. It is shared only with the service providers that run our e-mail, hosting and newsletter delivery, under contracts that limit its use, and with authorities where the law requires it. Data is stored on servers in the Russian Federation.
5. Your rights
Under Federal Law 152-FZ you may:
ask what data we hold about you and receive a copy;
have inaccurate data corrected;
withdraw consent and ask us to delete your data, unless we must keep it by law;
unsubscribe from the newsletter at any time using the link in the message.
6. Contact

Requests about personal data go to privacy@northgate-ind.ru or by post to Vorsino Industrial Park, plot 12, Borovsk District, Kaluga Region, 249020. We answer within 30 days. This policy may be updated; the current version is the one published on this page.

data.title: Four common mistakes in heavy machine foundation design
data.short_title: Four mistakes in heavy machine foundation design
data.lede: Get one dynamic load parameter wrong and the whole line can vibrate past its allowable limit within six months of operation.
data.excerpt: Field notes from 12 metalworking plants built over the past two years.

featured_image.alt: Four common mistakes in heavy machine foundation design

data.caption: Foundation works for a 1,600-tonne stamping press at the Elektra plant, Lipetsk SEZ.
data.author: Sergey Trofimov

children.text: A heavy machine foundation is not simply a bigger block of concrete. It is a vibrating system with its own natural frequency, and the designer’s job is to keep that frequency well away from the equipment’s operating range.
1. Taking dynamic loads from the catalogue instead of measuring them
Manufacturer figures are nominal values under ideal conditions. On presses and crushers, real amplitudes can run 20–40% higher once the tooling has worn.
Strengthening a badly designed foundation typically costs four times what a vibration survey would have cost before the pour.
2. Ignoring frost penetration and seasonal soil movement

In central Russia the design frost depth reaches 1.6 m and the groundwater table moves a metre or more between spring and autumn. That changes the subgrade modulus and pulls the foundation’s natural frequency towards resonance.
Survey the ground in both seasons for any machine above 500 tonnes.
Design against a range of subgrade moduli, not a single average value.
Show a contingency piling option on the drawings.
3. Tying the machine foundation into the building foundation
It saves a few dozen cubic metres of concrete, then transmits vibration into the columns and cracks the cladding within a year or two. Always provide a wide enough separation joint.

content.alt: Separation joint between machine and column foundations.
content.caption: Separation joint between machine and column foundations.

content.alt: Vibration measured with three accelerometers during commissioning.
content.caption: Vibration measured with three accelerometers during commissioning.

children.text: 4. Skipping vibration acceptance after commissioning
One measurement session with three accelerometers is enough to catch misalignment or under-torqued anchor bolts — before the line goes into real production.
